findings.claim: error_upsampling.py and organization_events_stats.py contain trailing-whitespace or whitespace-only lines. The repo's pre-commit trailing-whitespace hook rejects these lines.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py has whitespace-only lines (22, 28, 33, 36, 39, 49, 84) and a trailing space at line 51, and src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py has whitespace-only lines at 223, 234 and 278. All of them are added lines in the patch, and .pre-commit-config.yaml:179 turns on the trailing-whitespace hook for these paths.

findings.claim: The patch commits a stray `sentry-repo` submodule gitlink (mode 160000, commit a5d29095) at the repository root. It has no .gitmodules entry and is unrelated to the upsampling feature.

verifier.reason: change.patch:21-27 adds `sentry-repo` as a new mode-160000 gitlink pointing to commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. The repo root has no .gitmodules file and the patch does not add one, and the gitlink has nothing to do with the error-upsampling changes.

findings.claim: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in factories.py checks `if client_sample_rate:`. A valid client_sample_rate of 0 or 0.0 is therefore falsy and never set as sample_rate.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `if client_sample_rate:` in `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` (src/sentry/testutils/factories.py, around line 353, patch line 316). Because of that truthiness check, a client_sample_rate of 0 or 0.0 is skipped and `sample_rate` is never set.

findings.claim: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies client_sample_rate into sample_rate without production's checks. It skips the allowlist, type and 0<x<=1 range checks, swallows errors with a bare except, and lets invalid values reach the weighting logic.

verifier.reason: The test helper at src/sentry/testutils/factories.py:344-357 sets sample_rate = float(client_sample_rate) whenever the value is truthy. Production (src/sentry/event_manager.py:776-787) first requires the project to be allowlisted, the value to be an int or float, and 0 < x <= 1, so the helper accepts strings, negatives and values above 1. One detail is overstated: errors are swallowed by `except Exception: pass`, not a literally bare `except:`.

findings.claim: The 60s Django-cache layer in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects replaces the in-process-cached options.get with a network cache round trip. It also runs before the cheap dataset check, on every events-stats request.

verifier.reason: In error_upsampling.py (patch lines 153–166), `cache.get`/`cache.set` go to the Django cache (src/sentry/utils/cache.py:4) before the cheap `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` dataset check. `options.get` already serves values from an in-process local cache (src/sentry/options/store.py:132-163). `get_event_stats` calls this unconditionally on every events-stats request, including transactions and spans queries (patch lines 58–60).

findings.claim: The 60s per-org/project-set upsampling cache key does not include the allowlist contents, and nothing invalidates it when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes. A project removed from the allowlist keeps being upsampled until the entry expires.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py, the cache key is built only from the org id and a hash of the sorted project ids, with no allowlist contents in it, and the result is cached for 60s (patch lines 153 and 164). invalidate_upsampling_cache (error_upsampling.py:67) is never called anywhere in the repo, so after a project is removed from the allowlist it stays upsampled until the cache entry expires.

findings.claim: The allowlist lookup is a linear search per project instead of a set lookup.

verifier.reason: The new helper reads the allowlist as a list (option type=Sequence at src/sentry/options/defaults.py:3465) and then checks `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:58-63), so each project ID is found by scanning the list rather than by a set lookup. Allowlists and per-query project counts are small, so the cost is negligible.

findings.claim: The unit tests import and test private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform) and patch sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options. The public entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and its cache path are untested.

verifier.reason: The unit tests do import the private helpers and patch `options` (tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py:348-353, 378), but the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is not untested: the new endpoint tests (tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:503-621) run it through organization_events_stats.py:58 and check the upsampled versus normal counts on the cache-miss path. Only the cache-hit branch (error_upsampling.py:156-158) is never exercised on purpose.

findings.claim: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers and no option-change hook. It cannot work as designed, because cache keys are per (org, project-set) and an allowlist change cannot enumerate them.

verifier.reason: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:67-74) is never called anywhere in the repo, and nothing hooks the allowlist option. Its key needs the exact sorted project set (line 73, same as line 27), so an allowlist change cannot find every cached (org, project-set) entry to delete; only the 60s TTL at line 38 limits how long a stale result lasts.

findings.claim: The 'organization' parameter of _are_all_projects_error_upsampled is unused.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:43-64, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes `organization`, but the body only uses `project_ids` and the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. The caller at line 35 passes `organization`, and nothing reads it.

findings.claim: options.get(key, []) passes [] as the `silent` argument rather than as a default. The module also has a redundant `if not allowlist: return False`, a needless result variable, and `dataset` is typed Any instead of ModuleType.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:59, the `[]` in options.get(..., []) lands in the `silent` parameter, because the signature is `get(self, key: str, silent=False)` (src/sentry/options/manager.py:285). It has no effect because `[]` is falsy and the option already defaults to [] (src/sentry/options/defaults.py:3464-3467). The other points also hold: `if not allowlist: return False` (lines 60-61) is redundant because `all()` over non-empty project_ids already returns False, `result` (lines 64-65) is needless, and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` types `dataset` as Any (line 104) while the module types it as ModuleType elsewhere.

findings.claim: In OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint._get_event_stats, upsampling eligibility is computed from the outer `dataset` and raw request query instead of `scoped_dataset` and the executed query. As a result, dashboard-split subqueries (e.g. discover when the outer dataset is metrics) are not upsampled or are upsampled incorrectly.

verifier.reason: At src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py:220-222, eligibility is checked with the outer `dataset` and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`. The dashboard-split path only runs when `metrics_enhanced` is true (line 344), so the outer dataset is a metrics dataset and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False. That means the discover error subqueries at lines 363, 387 and 445 are never upsampled, even though `split_query`/`errors_only_query` exclude transactions.

findings.claim: _is_error_focused_query uses a plain substring test for 'event.type:error'. It matches negated ('!event.type:error') and OR'd queries, and misses variants like 'event.type: error'.

verifier.reason: The patch's new `_is_error_focused_query` in src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py lowercases the query and only checks `if "event.type:error" in query`, so it returns True for `!event.type:error` and for OR'd queries, and returns False for spaced variants such as `event.type: error`. The patch's tests (test_error_upsampling.py) cover only the positive, transaction and empty cases.

findings.claim: The upsampling cache keys are built with Python's built-in hash() of project IDs. hash() is process-dependent (PYTHONHASHSEED) and can collide, so keys do not match across workers and different project sets can share a key.

verifier.reason: The cache keys at error_upsampling.py (patch lines 153 and 199) hash `tuple(sorted(project_ids))`, and `project_ids` are ints (`Sequence[int]`). PYTHONHASHSEED only randomizes str/bytes hashes, so the hash of a tuple of ints is the same in every worker and keys do match across processes; a 64-bit collision between project sets is possible in theory but negligible in practice.

findings.claim: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null or zero handling. Errors lacking sample_weight in allowlisted projects count as 0.

verifier.reason: The patch defines upsampled_count as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no ifNull or default value (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py, patch lines 280-284), and its comments (patch lines 211-212, 278-279) say null handling was left out on purpose. Under SQL sum semantics a missing or NULL weight adds nothing, so those errors count as 0. If every row lacks it, the result could be NULL instead of 0, but the Snuba column schema is not in this repo to check.

findings.claim: The 'upsampled_count' SnQLFunction lambda has an unused parameter named 'args' instead of '_'.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py (patch hunk at ~line 1046), the new upsampled_count SnQLFunction uses `snql_aggregate=lambda args, alias: Function("toInt64", [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])], alias)`, so `args` is never used. The file mixes both styles: 6 of 37 `snql_aggregate` lambdas use `_`, so this is only a style nit.

findings.claim: upsampled_count in discover.py is not marked private=True. It is therefore exposed as a public Discover function that can bypass the allowlist and error-query checks and reference sample_weight on datasets without that column.

verifier.reason: The new SnQLFunction "upsampled_count" at src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041-1052 has no private=True, unlike its neighbours (e.g. column_hash at :1039). The builder only blocks private functions via is_accessible (builder/base.py:737), so any Discover user can put upsampled_count() in a query directly, skipping the allowlist and event.type:error checks in error_upsampling.py, and it sums sample_weight unconditionally.

findings.claim: upsampled_count uses default_result_type='number' while wrapping its result in toInt64() and replacing count(), which is 'integer'. Response metadata therefore reports a different type when upsampling is active.

verifier.reason: The patch adds upsampled_count in src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py (~line 1041). It wraps sum(sample_weight) in toInt64 but sets default_result_type="number", while the count() it replaces is declared with default_result_type="integer" (discover.py:251-258). transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling swaps count() for 'upsampled_count() as count' in organization_events_stats.py:233/277/296, so the 'count' field's metadata type changes from integer to number when upsampling is on.

findings.claim: Rewriting count() to 'upsampled_count() as count' changes the result column name. With transformAliasToInputFormat=1, process_results renames columns to 'upsampled_count() as count' while resolve_axis_column looks up 'count()', so the serializer emits 0.

verifier.reason: base.py:746 stores the full input string 'upsampled_count() as count' as FunctionDetails.field under alias 'count', so with the flag on, process_results (base.py:1566-1572) renames the result key to that string. organization_events.py:605-607 still resolves the axis from the original 'count()' (resolve_axis_column returns it unchanged at :75-76), so serializers/snuba.py:92 `r.get(column, 0)` returns 0.

findings.claim: The upsampling branch in the RPC path and in top-events is unreachable. use_rpc requires spans_rpc/ourlogs, for which _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False, and EAP RPC has no upsampled_count.

verifier.reason: `use_rpc` is true only when `dataset` is `spans_rpc` or `ourlogs` (organization_events_stats.py:204). The same outer `dataset` goes to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (line 220), and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for those datasets (error_upsampling.py, final `return False`), so the upsampled columns can never reach `run_timeseries_query` (lines 276-279) or `run_top_events_timeseries_query` (lines 232-236). One caveat: the top-events transform at line 232 sits before the `use_rpc` check, so it is still reachable on the non-RPC `top_events_timeseries` path for errors/discover; only its RPC use is dead.

findings.claim: The same transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling block is repeated in three mutually exclusive branches. upsampling_enabled is a pure alias of should_upsample.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py, the same `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block appears three times (lines 232-233, 276-277 and 295-296). Each sits in a branch that returns, so only one ever runs. `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` at line 226 just copies the value under a second name; both lines are added by the patch.
